first_impression.reaction: My assistant found this while we were looking at dates. The first screen is calm. No prices, no 'dream day', no packages, just seasons, official dates and covered spaces. It's a reference page though, not something written for a wedding our size. Her summary would be: 'Dry May to September, Nyepi 8 March 2027, only AYANA's ballroom (390) and Alila (250) can hold a big group under cover, nothing on exclusive use, security or private arrivals.' I read the takeaways, the March section, the covered spaces list, the questions and the close.

journey.quote: There is no single right time to get married in Bali.
journey.reaction: Understated. It doesn't try to sell me a month. Good start.

journey.quote: Nyepi falls on Monday 8 March 2027, beside the Idul Fitri holidays and collective leave, so ask your venue early how the day affects guests and suppliers.
journey.reaction: Useful. Half our guests would be travelling around Eid, so knowing Idul Fitri and Nyepi sit in the same week matters to my family more than the rain does.

journey.section: How to read BMKG's seasonal forecast for your year
journey.quote: A day under 5 mm is very light rain, 5 to 20 mm light, 20 to 50 mm moderate, 50 to 100 mm heavy and over 100 mm very heavy.
journey.reaction: Rainfall bands in millimetres. Someone else reads this for me. Skipped.

journey.section: Chapels and covered spaces, as each venue describes them
journey.quote: Its Amara Ballroom seats 390 for a ceremony.
journey.reaction: Finally a number that fits us. Everything else on the list is 25 to 90 people.

journey.section: Chapels and covered spaces, as each venue describes them
journey.quote: Notice the capacities. A chapel for 70 and a lawn for 250 suit very different guest lists, and the covered space needs to hold everyone, not only the ceremony.
journey.reaction: Right point. With 300 guests the rain plan is the real question, and the page knows it.

journey.quote: Ask which beach is safe for guests on the days around the wedding.
journey.reaction: Rip currents, dengue, rabies vaccines. This is written for a group chat of friends. Our guests' travel is handled for them.

journey.quote: Which covered space is held for you on the day, and does it seat your full guest list for both ceremony and dinner?
journey.reaction: Good question, but there's nothing about closing the property, screening from other hotel guests, or our security working with theirs. That's what my family office asks first.

journey.section: Larger guest lists travelling from Australia
journey.quote: A big group needs dates that work for flights, suppliers and covered space at once.
journey.reaction: The one section about large weddings assumes everyone is flying from Australia. We're Dubai, London and Sydney.

journey.section: Plan your month with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, and plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you.
journey.reaction: One contact suits me, fewer people means fewer leaks. But AUD and nothing showing a wedding at our scale.

unanswered_questions: Have you delivered a wedding for 200 to 400 guests in Bali, and can you show me one discreetly? (deferred business detail)
Do you arrange private airport arrivals, VIP transfers and coordination between our security team and the venue's? (deferred business detail)
Can you quote in a currency other than AUD, and work through a family office? (deferred business detail)
How do you handle confidentiality: NDAs, staff phones, press? (deferred business detail)
Can AYANA or any of these resorts be closed to the public, or a whole wing, for three days?
Which venues can cater halal for 300 guests during or around Idul Fitri and Idul Adha?
Which month gives the best chance of exclusive use, given resort occupancy across the year?

turn_offs_found.quote: Beach safety. Australians have drowned in rough seas and rip currents at popular beaches, including in Bali.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining traveller basics, and framed for Australians. It reads like a travel advisory, not wedding planning at my level.

turn_offs_found.quote: Health. Smartraveller notes dengue occurs in Bali and advises rabies vaccination before travel.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining. My guests' travel and health advice are handled by people whose job that is.

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, and plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you.
turn_offs_found.why: Quoting in AUD frames the service around Australian couples. I live in Dubai, so it tells me I'm outside the audience.

would_share_with: My assistant would keep the Nyepi and Idul Fitri dates, the AYANA Amara Ballroom 390 and Alila 250 figures and the covered-space questions in the planning file. Nobody else.

cta_reaction.why: I don't enquire through a blog link. The page is calm and accurate, but it says nothing about exclusive use, security, private arrivals or weddings our size, and it's written for Australians. I'd want a private introduction.

top_3_changes: Add questions to the venue list about exclusive use or closing spaces to other hotel guests, and about the couple's own security working with the venue's. Phrase them as questions to ask venues, not brand claims.

Rename 'Larger guest lists travelling from Australia' so it covers guests flying in from several countries, and note that Idul Fitri and Idul Adha matter for guests' own travel, not only supplier staffing.
Collapse the beach safety and health lines into a single pointer to Smartraveller for readers who delegate guest travel.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection

No invented brand facts; scale proof, transfers, security, currency and confidentiality listed in unanswered_questions as deferred
